newsitem.title: INDIA: India aims for 16 pct 97/98 money supply growth.
newsitem.headline: India aims for 16 pct 97/98 money supply growth.

text.p: India said on Friday it aimed to contain money supply growth in 1997/98 (April-March) within 16 percent.
India's money supply grew by 15.7 percent between January 19 in 1996 and January 17 this year.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told parliament in his budget for 1997/98 that the federal government will act in concert with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to cut fiscal deficit and money supply in order to contain inflation.
"Our goal is to break inflationary expectations and reduce the rate of inflation from the present level," he said in his budget speech.
India's inflation rate is currently at 8.0 percent.
